meta.dataDisclaimer: Prices verified as of update date. Actual prices may vary. Always verify current pricing before purchase.

scoringMethodology.valueScore: Price-to-performance ratio considering weight, durability, and features. Higher = better value.
scoringMethodology.weightScore: Inverse of weight relative to category average. 10 = ultralight, 5 = average, 1 = heavy.
scoringMethodology.durabilityScore: Expected lifespan and build quality. 10 = bombproof, 5 = typical, 1 = fragile.

insulation.name: Insulation Layer
insulation.description: Puffy jacket for camp and cold mornings

trekkingPoles.name: Trekking Poles
trekkingPoles.description: Support for knees, balance, and shelter pitching

items.name: Scout 55L
items.why: Entry-level pack with decent features. Great for testing if thru-hiking is for you before investing more.

items.name: Crown2 60
items.why: Best value ultralight-adjacent pack. Removable frame and lid let you customize weight. Proven on thousands of thru-hikes.

items.name: Exos 58
items.why: Best suspension in the lightweight category. Trampoline mesh back keeps you cool. Lifetime warranty.

items.name: Mariposa 60
items.why: Cottage brand classic. Half the weight of mainstream packs with full-featured design. Great for sub-20lb base weights.

items.name: Circuit
items.why: The cottage industry workhorse. Balances weight and durability perfectly. Can handle 30lb+ loads all day.

items.name: Arc Haul Ultra 60L
items.why: Lightest full-frame pack on market. Carbon fiber frame transfers load to hips. For serious gram-counters.

items.name: Southwest 55
items.why: Dyneema construction is virtually indestructible and fully waterproof. Premium materials justify the price for multi-year use.

items.name: Grand Mesa 2
items.why: Affordable freestanding tent that actually works. Heavy but reliable for budget hikers testing the waters.

items.name: Trail Hut 2
items.why: Best budget tent from REI. Thick floor, easy setup, and REI backing. Sweet spot for new hikers.

items.name: Flash Air 2
items.why: REI's ultralight entry. Can pitch with trekking poles to save 5oz. Great value for weight-conscious hikers.

items.name: Copper Spur HV UL2
items.why: Industry standard ultralight freestanding tent. Two doors, great livability, proven design.

items.name: X-Mid 1
items.why: Best value ultralight tent. Double-wall design solves condensation. Uses trekking poles. Cottage quality at mainstream price.

items.name: X-Mid 2
items.why: 2-person version of the beloved X-Mid. Palatial for solo hikers, reasonable weight for couples.

items.name: Duplex
items.why: Iconic ultralight shelter. Dyneema composite is lightest waterproof material. For dedicated gram counters.

items.name: Ozark Trail 40F Mummy
items.why: ⚠️ SUMMER SECTION HIKES ONLY. Not viable for NOBO thru-hikes - March temps can hit teens in Smokies. Use for testing or June+ starts only.

items.name: Celsius XXL 0°F
items.why: VIABLE budget bag for NOBO thru-hikes. 0°F rating handles March Smokies. Heavy at 4.5lbs but will keep you alive and warm.

items.name: Cosmic Down 20
items.why: Best budget down bag. 550-fill down at entry price. Great starter bag before going quilt.

items.name: Econ Burrow 20°
items.why: Budget cottage quilt. 850-fill duck down at remarkable price. Great entry to ultralight sleep systems.

items.name: Bandit 20°
items.why: Best value quilt on market. Cottage quality at mid-tier price. Customizable temp ratings and sizes.

items.name: Enigma 20°
items.why: EE's minimalist masterpiece. Sewn footbox saves weight. 850/950 fill options available.

items.name: Palisade 15°
items.why: Elite quilt with pad attachment system. No drafts, no fuss. Premium materials and construction.

items.name: NanoLite
items.why: Made in USA perfection. 850+ fill goose down. Will outlast multiple thru-hikes. The gold standard.

items.name: Z Lite Sol
items.why: Indestructible foam pad. Can't pop, always works. R-value 2.0 good for summer AT hiking.

items.name: Static V
items.why: Budget inflatable with surprising comfort. V-chamber design. Best bang for buck if you want air pad comfort.

items.name: Tensor Trail
items.why: Excellent value inflatable. 3.5" thick, R-value 2.8. Great balance of comfort and weight.

items.name: NeoAir XLite NXT
items.why: The benchmark ultralight pad. R-value 4.5 for 3-season use. 12oz with excellent warmth.

items.name: Tensor Elite
items.why: Lightest inflatable pad available. 8.5oz is foam territory with inflatable comfort.

items.name: MT100 Down Jacket
items.why: Best budget down jacket. Real down at unbelievable price. Perfect for hikers testing ultralight approach.

items.name: 650 Down Jacket 2.0
items.why: REI's value down jacket. 650-fill keeps costs down while providing real warmth. Good warranty.

items.name: Nano Puff
items.why: Synthetic insulation icon. Stays warm when wet unlike down. Ironclad warranty.

items.name: Ghost Whisperer/2
items.why: Benchmark ultralight down jacket. 800-fill at 8oz. Packs into own pocket. Worth the investment.

items.name: Primelite Pullover
items.why: Polish cottage brand ultralight specialist. 900-fill at 6.5oz. Hidden gem among gram counters.

items.name: Ultra-Lite2 Jacket
items.why: Disposable rain gear philosophy. $20 means you can trash it guilt-free. 5.5oz for jacket only.

items.name: Helium Rain Jacket
items.why: Ultralight hardshell that actually lasts. 2.5L construction, pit zips, hood that works.

items.name: Versalite Jacket
items.why: Japanese engineering at its finest. Gore-Tex Infinium at remarkable weight. Proven AT performer.

items.name: Norvan LT Hoody
items.why: Running-weight rain shell. Gore-Tex at under 5oz. For those who want the absolute lightest.

items.name: Lightweight Hiking Shoe
items.why: Budget trail shoe option. $35 at any Walmart nationwide. Waterproof, EVA midsole. Won't last 500 miles but perfect for section hikes or emergency replacement.

items.name: Lone Peak 8
items.why: THE AT standard trail runner. Wide toe box, zero drop, MaxTrac outsole. Most thru-hikers' choice.

items.name: Cascadia 18
items.why: Traditional drop alternative to Altras. Great for those who don't like zero drop. Proven on long trails.

items.name: Timp 5
items.why: More cushion than Lone Peak for rocky terrain. Ego Max midsole. Good for White Mountains PA rocks.

items.name: Speedgoat 6
items.why: Maximum cushion trail runner. Great for hikers with joint issues. Vibram Megagrip outsole.

items.name: BRS-3000T
items.why: Lightest canister stove at under 1oz. Titanium construction. Unbeatable for gram counters on budget.

items.name: WindMaster
items.why: Best wind performance in class. Micro-regulator technology. Reliable in any conditions.

items.name: PocketRocket 2
items.why: Industry standard canister stove. Reliable, fast, efficient. The benchmark all others are measured against.

items.name: 750ml Titanium Pot
items.why: Perfect size for solo hikers. Fits 110g fuel canister inside. Titanium = light and durable.

items.name: Sawyer Squeeze
items.why: THE thru-hike primary filter. Instant clean water, no waiting. 0.1 micron filtration, backflushable, virtually unlimited lifespan. 80%+ of AT thru-hikers use this.

items.name: BeFree 1L
items.why: Fastest flow rate filter for instant hydration. Lighter than Sawyer. Great primary choice but may need replacement mid-trail (1000L rating).

items.name: Aquamira Drops
items.why: BACKUP treatment only - not recommended as sole system. 30-minute wait means carrying more water and planning ahead. Essential backup when your filter breaks or freezes.
cons: Must carry untreated water while waiting

items.name: QuickDraw Microfilter
items.why: Good primary alternative to Sawyer. Faster flow than Squeeze, hollow fiber membrane. Great if you want options.

items.name: Tikkina
items.why: Most reliable budget headlamp. 300 lumens, uses AAA batteries (available everywhere). Petzl quality at entry price. Will get you to Katahdin.

items.name: NU25 (UL Version)
items.why: Ultimate ultralight headlamp. 1oz with USB-C charging. Red light mode for night hiking. The thru-hiker standard.

items.name: Actik Core
items.why: Rechargeable + AAA backup. 600 lumens with excellent beam. Trusted brand for reliability.

items.name: NB10000 Gen3
items.why: Best power-to-weight battery. 10000mAh at 5.3oz. Built-in cables eliminate carrying extras.

items.name: Nano Power Bank 10K
items.why: Budget-friendly 10000mAh power bank with built-in USB-C cable. 30W fast charging. Made from 80% recycled materials.

items.name: Ultralight/Watertight .3
items.why: Trail-ready first aid kit. Covers basics without bulk. Add personal meds and you're set.

items.name: Deuce #2
items.why: Ultralight aluminum trowel. 0.6oz and actually works. Leave No Trace essential.

items.name: Emergency Bivvy
items.why: Ultralight emergency shelter. Reflects body heat, fits in pocket. Better than space blanket.

items.name: Quick Lock Aluminum Poles
items.why: Best budget poles available. Cork grips, quick locks, and included baskets at an unbeatable price. Andrew Skurka approved.

items.name: Carbon Fiber Quick Lock Poles
items.why: Best value carbon poles. Same great CMT quality with lighter shafts. Used by thousands of thru-hikers.

items.name: Trail Back Poles
items.why: Most durable aluminum poles from a trusted brand. FlickLock Pro adjusters won't slip. Tank-like reliability.

items.name: Pursuit Poles
items.why: Best overall trekking pole. Carbon upper, aluminum lower combines light weight with durability. Editors Choice winner.

items.name: Distance Carbon FLZ
items.why: Best foldable trail running poles. 3-section Z-fold packs to 15 inches. Great for fastpacking.

items.name: LT5 Poles
items.why: Ultra-lightweight carbon poles from cottage brand. Sub-11oz pair. For dedicated gram counters.

items.name: Crux Carbon Poles
items.why: Lightweight 3-section foldable poles at great price. EVA grips, carbon shafts. Great for trekking pole tents.

items.name: Hiker Micro Crew
items.why: THE thru-hiking sock standard. Lifetime warranty means free replacements forever. Merino wool comfort.

items.name: Liner Crew
items.why: Toe sock specialists. Prevents between-toe blisters. Great as liner with outer sock or standalone.

items.name: Light Hiker No Show
items.why: Light cushion version for warm weather. Same lifetime warranty. Good for trail runners.

items.name: Hike Classic Edition
items.why: Classic merino wool hiking sock. Medium cushion, good availability. Slightly cheaper than Darn Tough.

items.name: Max Patch Crew
items.why: 100% American-made merino. Named after AT shelter. Great alternative to Darn Tough with lifetime warranty.

items.name: Athletic Crew 6-Pack
items.why: ⚠️ EMERGENCY ONLY - Cotton blend WILL cause blisters. Only use if you lose all socks mid-trail and need same-day replacement. Replace with merino ASAP.

items.name: Trail Sock 4-Pack
items.why: BEST BUDGET MERINO. 72% merino wool at $4.50/pair. Made by same factory as premium brands. Costco membership required but worth it.

items.name: Merino Wool Hiking Crew
items.why: Affordable merino from REI. 67% merino wool, lifetime satisfaction guarantee. Great budget option without Costco membership.
